content:
The future of our nation (and the game) is in your hands.

Please feel free to make overly impassioned speeches.

Types of government include:

A true democracy: Every issue is voted on by every person. 
Pro: The individual gets a hand in shaping the future.
Con: The court of public opinion will directly change how the government works.
Wealth: capitalistic.

A republic: A group of people represent the rest of the people and take care of the issues.
Pro: An organized group of people with checks and balances govern and can be removed from power.
Con: The group of people will be easily influenced by the people with the most money.
Wealth: Capitalistic

A monarchy: A single leader holds wealth and provides goods to those who provide services. The nation gets divided in to a feudal system where each state is it's own kingdom.

Pro: With enough violence you can become king. And then claim that a higher power wants your child and every firstborn there after also be a king.
Con: You likely wont be a king.
Wealth: Centralized by taxation.

Socialism: Everything belongs to the government to be redistributed to everyone equally. A group of leaders controls the infrastructure. From roads to manufacturing, every part of life is controlled by the rulers.

Pros: Life generally gets taken care of for you, and people are generally treated as equals. A farmer is paid the same as a doctor.
Cons: There is a cap on how successful you can be before the government owns what you have made to distribute it as common property. 
Wealth: Individual with a cap.

Communism: Everything belongs to everyone, and there is no social class system. The country is united with no political parties. Everyone has a job and an education.

Pro: No one is born with a material advantage over you. Everyone starts life equal. There is no wealthy elite. Your bills will be non existent.

Con: A centralized government which controls all of the wealth of a state can be corrupted into think of the state as their opportunity for capitalism. Because all science, manufacturing, military and agriculture is controlled by one entity, it is essentially an all powerful government that can wield the countries' resources any way it chooses.  

Wealth: none.

Oligarchy: The purist form of capitalism, the country is literally controlled by companies.

Pro: Science, technology manufacturing and agriculture are typically at the forefront and highly competitive  and advancements are the focus.

Con: There is a rigid caste system that forces the average worker to be impoverished and dependent on the company for both goods and wealth. Wealth is seen as the most important feature of a person's life.

Wealth: Low potential for high wealth. 

Meritocracy: A system of government in which the most qualified are the ruling class. Every job, every penny you earn is based on your ability to do that job.

Pro: Ideally the people most competent at running the country will do so. As will every major position.

Con: for those on the lower half of the bell curve of being skilled, you are valueless unless you improve.
@everyone Welcome to liberty hall: Please feel free to add your opinion. (Npcs are welcome too) . I understand that my descriptions are inadequate and reduced considerably. this is intentional.
You come upon a gathering place in the city of Philo.
This is a town hall meeting where anyone can have a voice.
Please come in character and decide the fate of Arcania.
Once your have picked the form of government we will use it to select the first ruller(s) of Arcania. Good luck.

whenever this canonically happens Bones takes a seat and puffs his pipe. "every man should be entitled to the sweat of his brow, and how hard he fights for something. the people who have worked the hardest have been stomped on by a buncha NINNIES who've never known a day of hard work in their life. the people who actually built this city are still stuck in the slums and the wastes under the crown even though WE have been bled dry so everyone here has a place, has a railroad, has any of this fancy machinery. I can show you where the bones of this city are and not one of them have people stopped to thank or pay a respect to! Because they don't parade around or shout for an idea, they spend every day busting their backs making it through the next day. It's good to take care of your brother, or the people who aren't able to put in that work, but heaven above and hell below if hard work doesn't earn you the right to choose in your life than you don't live at all and you're already dead. my votes meritocracy, if someone has a problem with anything that gets in place, that's fine, outdo the guy you disagree with. EARN IT" at the end he heavily sets his sledge across the table. "I've died three times for this city. This is the way"

A white raven takes that into consideration. "'Take care of people who aren't able to put in work', I agree. All your points really. I want us to live in an Arcania where people are given what they need. No one should live without. Everyone deserves that much."

"I don't know what kind of government I'm idealizing, so I'll just offer my points. No one should live without but I agree those who have worked for it should be allowed to live with what they've earned. *They* who worked for it. I don't want to see anyone's rightfully earned coin in the pockets of people whose only claim to the money is that they're higher on the ladder. They won't even use the coin for anything worthwhile, anything good. The redcoats stole our silver and funneled them into things that would only harm the people of Empire City, the innocent werefolk that live with us. I don't want that."
Bo, the unofficial ambassador of the were folk, sits in a chair off to the side taking notes.
Finn and his 3 retainers come inside. Finn is dressed in his simple patriotic gear rather than the full star spangled get up

“Theydies and gentlethems, think of this as an opportunity to make something new, not just pick a form that has been cut and dried with inherent flaws. We can take the best parts of what we see.
Broaden your perspectives and imagine. Bits and bobs of a Democratic-Socialist-Republic.


- Term Limits on all positions
- Representative and proportional elections
- Welfare programs to take care of extreme class divisions, inequalities and great privileges
- Individualism and Free Will including speech, assembly, beliefs, life choices!

Most importantly, checks making sure public servants in elected positions stay just that. No profiting from a position of power. Having them make the minimum wage of the country and be dedicated to bettering the lives of the people they represent! Oh and none of that company campaign donations or other ways to insert dark money, we could create a system where candidates share an equal pool to campaign with if they even do.

But all in all I would describe this as a Midaskian government solution. Checks and balances in a representative and equal government!”
"It's a working point so there's always room for more, but this is the gist of it" He gives a wide smile

Irynx raises her wing. "Maybe we can remove re-elections altogether. Probably the only part of a monarchy I'd like to keep, save for the names. I mean, being called 'Your Highness' is really fancy and I won't deny that. But anyway my point is, if we put someone in power, I want to see them using all the time they have with it doing their best and not obsessing over how to get the people to fall in love with them again."
"We give them only one election term to make a difference!" He says in agreement
(edited cuz you said re-elections and I misread)

"A lifetime can be impractical though. And Elf or a Dwarf that lives for hundreds of years compared to a dragonborn or teifling who have such short lifespans. I would like to see some sort of limit on leadership terms."
"5 Years seem good? Or 10 if you really hate math and guessing when the election year is"
"I hate math, let's do it."
"10 years I think is a suitable amount of time for someone to make so positive and lasting influence and change. Projects on the level of a nation can take a long time to complete."

"10 years is also a suitable amount of time for someone to subvert our systems and seize control over the country. Projects do take a while to do, that's why we have the next leaders to continue the work."

"One person wouldn't have all the power to do that, but the hope is that representatives that do represent the beliefs of the people could indeed make the change the majority would want, or at least make compromises for progress"

There are other reasons I think why 10 years is too long of an election cycle. Public opinion changes quite often, why look at us. It didn't take months, but weeks for us to undergo radical changes. If representatives are meant to represent majority opinions, then we should check to see if they are still doing so. A term duration of 5 years coupled with a two term limit, would give the same effect as 1 10 year term but wouldn't force us to wait 10 years to remove a leader who has lost our confidence.

"I like the idea of a 5 year limit with a max of two terms. If the people like them, they will have a lot of time to stay in office but if the people no longer agree with the path they have set we don't have to follow through with it.'

"And the point of campaigning was brought up a while ago. If everyone has the same resources in campaigning, a point I agree with, re-election wouldn't weight too much on the current sovereign's mind. Their actions will have to speak for themselves.
Vivica nods "They will be placed on an even playing field and will have to rely on merit and their own works to succeed."

"As someone who's lived a long time, ten years feels like nothing. As someone who's been in this city for the past month, so much can happen that ten years feels like forever."

"I still disagree with the two-term thing. I don't think people should get a do-over for something as important as the leadership of Arcania. And if everyone's so sure they can do good with more years, then why don't they use the time they already have?"
"It is not a do-over, only a continuation of what they already have done. If the current leader fails their first term, public opinion will not grant them a second."

Finn listens and agrees with the two terms max limit
"Great points both, but I think by mitigating any special interests and having them share campaign funds, elections would be based on the values of the people. 10 I guess is some people's lifetimes, 5 would give greater access to voting for more people"
"I wouldn't call it a do over, more as like we've liked what they've done thus far and would like to see more from them as a leader."
The Speaker nods at Vivica.
"The two terms also gives folk with smaller life spans to have more say on their leadership."
"Split the difference. Midterm election?"
"You wish to cut 5 into 2 and a half years?"
"I think it's referring to agreeing on a 5 year term with 2 terms max"
"Yeah, that's what split the difference means. We're disagreeing, so we're making a compromise."
The speaker nods at this. He goes silent once more as he meditates internally on his opinions for government.
"Like you know, five years are up and now everyone gets to decide if this person is fit to continue up to their ten years on the council or whatever it is we're making up."
"Excellent! I love this new form of government already"
Kegbot sits in and listens taking notes on what seems to be liked.
"What do we do about someone that is corrupt and manages to get into the role. Is there a way to have everyone agree to change them out before the term has ended?" The more monotoned robot speaks.

"Checks and balance! Midaskian government form would absolutely have votes of no confidence in some capacity, whether as individuals granting some sort of majority of population, or elected officials having a super majority to oust them!"
"Do we have any limit on how many people are allowed to .... want to become public servants?"
"How about three in the executive branch, and proportionate to population in both Judicial and Legislative?"
"Hmm three is good, but in a majority rule election how do we pick the three people, will their positions be elected separately?"
"How would power be divided between the three of them?"

"They function as a democracy. Each branch would. All running in the same election for same position, but of the pool of candidates, with ranked voting, it would be proportional to representing the people!"
"My questions were for the three who would be elected into the executive branch."
"Ranked voting"
"1st 2nd and 3rd places"
"Rule of three. That's a good one. Why do you think hag covens always come in threes? Because they'd kill each other, obviously, but it's a good system in general."
Vivica nods thinking this over "It would prevent stalled decision making with opposing opinions there will always be a third voice in the room..."

(unfortunately this has to be in two messages because lol I should not be allowed to type)

"||This is gonna be a ride...||" Roy thinks to himself before starting talking.
"Friends of all appearances, if I may add add to the discussion with my experiences. My name is Roy Gat Bivur - that is, given name Roy, of the Gat family, from the Bivur swarm. I'm a swarmkeeper from the old world, from the communities living together with colonies of insects."

"Where I'm from, among the communities of the greater swarm, here's how things work: each community is mostly self-governing, and its common insect colony is a slightly different variant of the greater swarm, more fitting for their environment. Each community sends representants to the gatherings where matters affecting all communities are discussed. Now, would I speak in favor of using exactly the same for Arcania? No."

"The problem with it was that eventually it regressed to several families calling the shots, regardless of whether they're fit for it. And the Gat family has been one of such. Which is why I was sent across the ocean to start seeking means of refuge for the greater swarm in case the wars consume our communities. Not because I was the best for the task - because my family wanted to make sure my brother's the one to take over after them, and keep things the way they've been."

"What I'm saying is, there is value in doing things that way - who'll know better what let's say one community needs, people from it, or ones from a completely different environment? But at the same time, this is delicate balance that requires care. While I agree with the points you've been making so far, I want to point to what our friend Bones has been saying as source of wisdom, and caution."

"While I agree that we need the best among us to lead, I don't believe merit equals merit - I don't think I'd trust someone like myself to be in charge of, say, health of the citizens. But, at the same time, those closest to the common folk, working hard for themselves, their families, and communities, should definitely have their voice heard and considered, maybe even followed."

"With that context, to what you've been discussing, I'd like to suggest the following: no leaders should be all-powerful, because no mortal person can know everything. Let us have someone that would coordinate everything, yes, but accompanied by those best in their field to provide everything one needs to make decisions. Example, let's say, about teachers. One to be in charge of schooling would have to have experience in it. One who has never experienced it from both the student and teacher perspective, shouldn't decide on things that don't affect them."

"But, this too would need careful tending to, of course. Following just that, we'd eventually go back to square one, with only the old and established deciding, and influencing anyone new to follow the exact same path. No progress, only past. So I suggest that each body in charge of a specific area has both the experienced and established, and those currently affected by it. No one or two or three people can ever have a complete picture. Swarms, machines, and communities are all alike. There might be one central part making decisions like ones you're discussing, but these decisions come based on what other parts experience. Does that make sense?"

"Your experience and words are valid and wise my friend. I like it! Responsibilities would fall to qualified candidates that are elected into their positions within the branches, or are independently placed into the cabinet as experts in related fields"

Vivica listens to Roy and nods, taking in his words "The best qualified should lead, I agree, of the best qualified the people should choose their leaders, the ones they find the most qualified. Experts in their field should hold influence over their domain but I also think their word or opinion shouldn't be final. I might not know much about magic but I understand basic ethics regarding using enchantments on people."
"Absolutely right. We trust the people who we know can do the job right."

The Mender stands up "As this is a formal address.... I assume proper names are a something to use... Last time I was here.... I was known as The Honorable Judge, Baron Sandigill, Eldest Chinnokin of the Roanoak Colony and Priest of the Twin Vents School, Member of the Mid Atlantic Nation.  Most of that title is meaningless now..." He thinks for a moment "These days... I guess my proper  name now would just be Mender Sandigill of Murry Hill."  He has a pensive look at he takes a moment to look out a window, and pulls out a bag of good berries from her vest and eats one.  After a moment he continues "I have some wisdom... or maybe a warning... to pass on.  I have seen suggestions of divided power.  Last time.... we tried that.  Every decision.... every need.... bogged down in bureaucracy.  Every decision was discussed.... and discussed.... and questioned..... almost to the point that the town couldn't get along.  The divisions... the fractures.... caused by loyalties to one person or another..... meant very little got done.  That was 5 people managing a town of maybe 100.  I lost my life to their indecision.... their inability to work togeather.  The work we did.... is lost to time.  I believe they won after my passing.... as I don't think I could even be here had they failed."  He eats another goodberry.  
He shakes his head and continues "A leader must be able to act... to react.  The more people that are involved in making a decision.... the more time everything takes.... and the more room for corruption to seep in.  If you have 1 leader.... either that person is corrupt or not.  With 100 people making decisions.... all you need are half to be greedy.... self serving... to corrupt your process.  You don't even need that.  5 or 10 people can convince 40 or 50 to corruption.  It's easier to identify 1 corrupt person on a pedestal than it is 5 in a crowd."
He pauses once more collecting his thoughts "We **have** seen good kings in history... single people that have lead their people well. Single people that love and provide for their people.   And when we see the like of *King George III* the people rise up.... fight.  You don't have to depend on dividing the power to save the people.  You have to depend on good people to stand up to a corrupt leader.  And that is easier with a single person wearing the target.  I won't tell you the best way to run your new country... but I will suggest that you look to the fallen republic of Greece.... the fall of the triumvirate in Rome.... if you want to see what splitting the power does."
he takes one more moment to eat another goodberry "I have seen the very souls of the people here.... everyone has the potential to do wrong.... but I would say most of your hearts are i the right place.  I think Roy has some good points.... I think elections are smart.... beyond that.... You might consider a leader and cabinet of experts approach..." he pauses one last time "This is your new world... so I can't tell you what is best.  You have to consider the native tribes that live here... the war on the other side of the ocean.... the immigrants that are here.... and continue to move here.... and decide if you want a better world today.... or wait for many voices to waste time deciding on what first step to take.... So at least consider the boons of a single leader... for I have witnessed that failure of split government first hand."  he says.  Then quietly goes to an edge of the room to sit down."

"Five people to a hundred feels like a wrong ratio. I can see why it got messy. But Arcania's a big world. Power proportionate to the population or uh, whatever Captain Midask said. Maybe instead of dividing the power, we divide Arcania, in some way. A single leader and their cabinet in charge of a microkingdom, and we have many of those little countries all a part of Arcania."

"Like the swarm communities. I'm not denying the need for swift decision every now and then - only that the decisions should have some reason behind them. I'd say it still fits what I suggested, those with experience or first-hand knowledge present the situation, problem, and maybe even some suggestion for a solution. Those good at coordinating people's efforts and making decisions coordinate from the top. Right people are still in their right places in this image."

"It all needs to be worth of trust. The more people feel like they have to question their fellows, the more will be spent on talking. In an airship, everyone has their post, after all. You can help a crewmate if needed, you can check on them if things look dire, but you trust the pilot is piloting, the gunner has their finger on the trigger, and you make sure the engines all roar. For example, at least. With a captain coordinating everyone to let them do their part. It's not five captains, it's a crew. That's how I'm seeing it, regarding the concerns."

Roy scratches the back of his head. "Not like 'worth of trust' is something that can be easily codified, I suppose."

"I get your metaphor but in an airship, anyone can step up and be captain when needed. Then again, that's not bad. Even if everyone is specialized in a certain thing, and anyone can be a captain when they need to be, the person trained to be the captain is the best person for captain."

"Captain, captain, captain," she repeats a few more times just to take away the meaning of the word further.

"Both a strength and a weakness. Anyone can take over, but not everyone needs to. And as a captain, you must recognize both your strengths and weaknesses, and your crew's, after all. You let the crew do their things, you refer to the gunner about the targetting, you ask the pilot if they have enough engine power, you make decisions based on that. Sometimes someone of your crew might know better. But as a crewmate, one must trust that the captain *will* notify you when your voice will matter the most, and you don't disrupt others just for your time on the stage. Delicate balance."

"And you're right, the more I say that the less it sounds like a word. Is it like that too when I talk about the swarm?"
"Swarm." The raven nods.

"I agree with the Mender. We can argue systems no matter what, but at the end of the day our government's efficacy will be determined by whomever stays in power. If we have a way to guarantee a good person as our ruler, even a dictatorship would yield benefits for our nation. Elections was our answer to the question of who to lead, but I implore us to look at other answers. Beings like the ravens," He looks towards Irynx with a dry, curt nod. "who possess a plethora of knoweldge might give us proper insight to who can lead. It's also not just the ravens, there are other beings and magics out there that might be used." His tarot deck glows slightly at this. "Maybe, there is no need for elections and a much swifter solution might be put in place."

"I'd welcome advice and insight from anyone with relevant knowledge, but I'd be cautious with just leaving everything to powers beyond mortal. Gods of the old world are such powers too, and I don't suppose wars between them are something that should spill over to this shore."

"I'd be cautious with leaving everything to them as well. I'm simply proposing asking for help and guidance. They are already serving as protectors, why not ask for their expertise in leading as well. And the ravens aren't the only ones we can approach."
Grimlock roars as if to nominate herself.

Finn takes in the points before speaking
"I read about the division of labor in the Roanoke colony. They split the power into three different jobs. An ambassador, mayor, and captain of the guard of sorts. Their biggest failure was in their communication and lack of meetings. A group of 3 that concern themselves only with leading and not with adventuring as well seems like it would dilute that problem. 

As for the ravens or other divine beings. Sure they may be useful guardians and can be personally sought after for help, but I definitely want them to have no part in shaping the future of the world if we can help it. A complete separation of church and state. For those that don't follow the ravens for example, I wouldn't want the country's policies to be something a non believer would have to adhere to. Whomever is elected into power can seek out that guidance on their own time, but I don't want our system of government to rely on a godlike being. They die, squabble, war, and fight each other for power over domains. That's a headache we don't need."
